purpose: Progressive-disclosure manifest for one governed Freedom 250 research package.
title: The military gained border-land arrest power, not control of civilian courts
question: How does the military acquire protective and arrest authority over National Defense Areas, and does that process extend military jurisdiction over Federal offices or civilian courts?
bluf: The executive branch has expanded the military-property perimeter by transferring selected Federal border lands to War Department administrative control, attaching them to existing bases and invoking installation-protection law. Designated personnel may arrest civilians for NDA-linked offenses and, under an August 2026 OLC opinion, pursue them just beyond the boundary before civilian handoff. Civilians remain in civilian custody and U.S. district court; no blanket military authority over Federal offices or changed judicial-district boundary was found.
evidence_cutoff_note: Official presidential, land-transfer, military, statutory, OLC, court and prosecution records checked through October 12, 2026. Nonpublic section 2672 designations, Attorney General-approved guidelines, arrest-level actor data and a complete six-area prosecution census were not retrieved.
use_note: Read the process in order: presidential mission, land transfer, installation annex, restricted-area order, personnel designation, arrest, civilian handoff and ordinary district-court prosecution. Do not collapse administrative land jurisdiction into legislative jurisdiction, military custody into trial jurisdiction, or a DOJ OLC opinion into a court holding.
